claims.claim: Jiang explicitly tells the class to use imagination, signaling that the scenario should be judged as a thought experiment rather than dismissed because its psychology feels implausible.
A student-parent says that in real life he would first sit down with Eve and try to understand her motives before deciding what to do next.
Jiang answers that he can imagine this kind of testing behavior from children and uses his own experience as a father of three to defend the metaphor's plausibility.
The therapy-defending student argues that parents already outsource essential forms of care like food and water, so using trained help for a child's mind should not count as abandonment.
Jiang challenges the authority of therapy by asking why a stranger with a PhD should be assumed to know more about the child than the parent does.
The student answers that trained therapists know more than parents about behavioral patterns even if they do not know everything about the child.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang openly refuses the class's realism complaints and forces them back into imaginative participation.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Again, we need to use our imagination.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It captures the methodological pressure of the lecture: the thought experiment is supposed to reveal a logic of redemption, not survive as a child-psychology case study.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang grounds the wild metaphor in ordinary family life by saying any of his own children could try a smaller version of this emotional blackmail.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I have three kids. And any of them could pull this crap on us.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This keeps the packet from reading like pure abstraction and shows how Jiang links theology to intimate parental testing.

signature_moments.moment: The argument condenses into a direct challenge to expert mediation: why trust the stranger with the PhD over the parent who bears the relationship?
signature_moments.source_phrase: a stranger with a PhD knows more about the child than you, the parent
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's sharpest formulation of Jiang's anti-delegation pressure and sets up the next move toward divine outsourcing analogies.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The class uses outsourcing help to name the dispute over whether professional expertise can stand in for parental responsibility without changing what the child learns about love.

chronology_notes.note: This 2026-06-16 packet moves from realism objections back into Jiang's imaginative method, then sharpens the debate into a direct contest between parental intimacy and credentialed behavioral expertise.
